L716: IV. D ISCUSSION
L717: 
L718: Our experiments indicate that more precise time and energy
L719: 
L720: measurement systems with calibrations can improve measure-
L721: 
L722: ment accuracy. Higher bandwidth (>2 GHz) oscilloscopes can
L723: reduce the deformation of the echo signal. Data acquisition
L724: 
L725: system with a higher time resolution can provide ﬂight time
L726: 
L727: measurements more accurately. To achieve hyperspectral mea-
L728: 
L729: surements, a grating method could be considered as a substitute
L730: 
L731: for the current spectral ﬁlter. A Cassegrain telescope could
L732: 
L733: also improve the efﬁciency of the optical system, increase
L734: 
L735: the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and enlarge the measurement
L736: 
L737: distance. Because of the inconsistencies of the supercontin-
L738: uum laser pulse energy and inconsistencies in the sensitivity
L739: 
L740: of the APD module, calibrations should be conducted in the
L741: 
L742: future.
L743: 
L744: When the optical portion is driven by a two-axis rotary,
L745: 
L746: the system can be conﬁgured to produce a 3-D point cloud,
L747: 
L748: where each point has both a distance and a plurality of spectral
L749: 
L750: band reﬂectivity information. The inversion of structural and
L751: 
L752: biochemical parameters can be developed from 2-D to 3-D.
L753: 
L754: However, both the instability of supercontinuum laser power
L755: and the small diameter of the refracting telescope may result
L756: 
L757: in a lower receiving sensitivity and SNR. Additionally, the
L758: 
L759: oscilloscope used for the high-speed analog/digital conversion
L760: 
L761: and data collection may decrease the efﬁciency of the test in
L762: 
L763: outdoor environments.
L764: 
L765: In the future, we will evaluate the system for the estimation
L766: 
L767: of biochemical parameters for vegetation [18]. Our approach
L768: 
L769: should be further veriﬁed using larger data sets and be ex-
L770: tended to more complex conditions. Hyperspectral LiDAR with
L771: 
L772: an extended distance and a wider spectral range will greatly
L773: 
L774: improve the efﬁciency for monitoring the vertical distribution
L775:

L780: A four-wavelength multispectral LiDAR prototype system

L925:   * cite21†Simin Chen L926:   * cite22†Shaojing Song L927:   * cite23†Yicheng Wang L928:   * cite24†Yuwei Chen L929: In the fields of agriculture and forestry, the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is a critical indicator for assessing the physiological state of plants. Traditional imaging sensors can only collect two-dimensional vegetation distribution data, while dual-wavelength LiDAR technology offers the capability to capture vertical distribution information, which is essential for forest structure recovery and precision agriculture management.
L930: However, existing LiDAR systems face challenges in detecting echoes at two wavelengths, typically relying on multiple detectors or array sensors, leading to high costs, bulky systems, and slow detection rates. This study introduces a time-stretched method to separate two laser wavelengths in the time dimension, enabling a more cost-effective and efficient dual-spectral (600 nm and 800 nm) LiDAR system.
L931: Utilizing a supercontinuum laser and a single-pixel detector, the system incorporates specifically designed time-stretched transmission optics, enhancing the efficiency of NDVI data collection. We validated the ranging performance of the system, achieving an accuracy of approximately 3 mm by collecting data with a high sampling rate oscilloscope. Furthermore, by detecting branches, soil, and leaves in various health conditions, we evaluated the system’s performance.
L932: The dual-wavelength LiDAR can detect variations in NDVI due to differences in chlorophyll concentration and water content.
